units.source_text: 那时，火与火互相亲近了。

en.t: At that time, fire drew close to fire.

units.source_text: 火不会像现在这样被分截、被贬低，火总是能够同别的火携起手来，纠合成无数的火。

en.t: Fire was not divided and diminished as it is now; fire could always join hands with other fires and gather into countless flames.
Perhaps people are like that too.

units.source_text: 火不论在哪里，都能够召唤别的火，它的呼声很快地传达到了。

en.t: Wherever fire was, it could call to other fires, and its cry was quickly carried to them.

units.source_text: 各个寺庙的被焚，全是由于失火、连遭火灾或是战火所致，并没有留下纵火的记录。

en.t: The burning of the various temples was all caused by accidental fires, repeated conflagrations, or the flames of war, and no records of arson were left behind.

units.source_text: 即使古时某个时代有像我这样的男子汉，他也只能是屏住气息。

en.t: Even if, in some age of the past, there had been a man like me, he could only have held his breath.
Taixian waited for the right moment.

units.source_text: 各个寺庙有如一日一定会被焚毁的。

en.t: It was as if every temple was certain to be burned down one day.

units.source_text: 只要等待，钻空子的火就一定会相继而起，火与火就一定会携手完成它应该完成的使命。

en.t: If one only waited, fires that seized their chance would surely rise one after another, and fire would join with fire to fulfill the mission it was meant to fulfill.

units.source_text: 实际上，金阁只不过是由于罕见的偶然才免于火灾。

en.t: In reality, the Golden Pavilion escaped fire only through a rare accident of chance.

units.source_text: 火自然而起，灭亡和否定是常态，建造起来的寺庙一定会被焚毁，佛教的原理和规则是严密地支配着人间的。

en.t: Fire arises naturally; destruction and negation are the normal state; temples that have been built are certain to be burned down, and the principles and rules of Buddhism govern the human world with strict precision.

units.source_text: 即使是纵火，那也是过分地诉诸自然、诉诸火的各种力量。

en.t: Even if it is arson, it is an excessive appeal to nature and to the various powers of fire.

units.source_text: 所以历史学家无论谁都不把它当做纵火来看待。

en.t: That is why no historian treats it as arson.
